name: Fernando 2006
question: Does immediate overlapping external anal sphincter repair reduce fecal incontinence at 12 months compared with end-to-end repair after obstetric sphincter injury?

arms.label: Immediate primary overlapping external anal sphincter repair
immediate primary end-to-end external anal sphincter repair

design.population: 64 women with acute obstetric grade 3b or 3c anal sphincter injury or fourth-degree perineal tear; grade 3a and prior third- or fourth-degree tears excluded.
design.description: Single-center randomized trial; allocation minimized for parity, gestation, and delivery mode; two trained clinicians performed repairs
design.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 1262–1264; Table 1, p 1266

verdictNote: Primary fecal incontinence differed at 12 months among 52 of 64 questionnaire respondents.
takeaway: Among 52 women assessed at 12 months after immediate obstetric sphincter repair, fecal incontinence occurred in 0/27 after overlap versus 6/25 (24%) after end-to-end repair (RR 0.07, 95% CI 0.00–1.21; P = .009).

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give June 2006 only; first day of month used for the required ISO date
reports.citation: Fernando RJ, Sultan AH, Kettle C, et al. "Repair techniques for obstetric anal sphincter injuries: a randomized controlled trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2006;107(6):1261-1268. doi:10.1097/01.AOG.0000218693.24144.bd
reports.followUp: Questionnaires at 6 weeks and 3, 6, and 12 months after repair; 52/64 returned the 12-month questionnaire

results.measure: Women reporting fecal incontinence at 12 months
results.note: Reported as an intention-to-treat analysis, but 12-month outcomes use 52/64 questionnaire respondents; prespecified two-sided alpha was .05. The published RR interval includes 1 despite P = .009.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1264–1265; Table 2, p 1266

results.measure: Women reporting fecal urgency at 12 months
results.note: The 12-month urgency analysis included 52/64 randomized women.

results.measure: Women reporting deterioration from 6 weeks to 12 months
Women reporting flatus incontinence at 12 months

harms.label: Blood transfusion, wound dehiscence, fistula formation, or suture migration
harms.note: The paper did not report Clavien-Dindo grades, retention, infection, or reoperation rates.

delivery.label: Repair timing and approach
delivery.value: Within 3 hours of injury detection, two trained clinicians performed repairs under regional or general anesthesia. End-to-end repair used 2–3 mattress sutures of 3-0 PDS; overlap used two suture rows after mobilization, dividing remaining EAS fibers when needed. Torn IAS was repaired separately with interrupted 3-0 PDS.

delivery.label: Median operating time and estimated blood loss
delivery.note: Time P = .003 in Results (.03 in Discussion); blood loss P = .05.

delivery.label: Postoperative antibiotic and bowel regimen
delivery.value: All women received intraoperative IV antibiotics, oral antibiotics for 7 days, and ispaghula husk plus lactulose for 14 days.
